title: Why Duke fired Bubber Miley, and Duke's hands-off style
summary: Bubber was the only man Duke fired, for being absent when big shots came; Duke never told Cootie what to play.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: And that was just Tricky's own thing. He just -- that was him. He didn't get it from anybody, did he?
No. Not as I knowed of. Not unless he got it from Bubber. I don't know.
Oh, I see. Yeah. Yeah. But Bubber didn't sound exactly like that, anyway, did he?
I don't know. I never heard Bubber play in person.
I didn't either.
I never heard him play in person. I heard him on the radio. But I never heard him play in person.
You said Duke fired Bubber. I didn't know Duke ever fired anybody.
That's the only man he ever fired in his life.
No kidding. Well, how -- I know Bubber was wild.
The reason why he fired Bubber Miley was every time someone big shot come up to listen to the band, there wasn't no Bubber Miley. And he had the whole band built around Bubber Miley.
Yeah.
And maybe he decided, he says, "Well, this man has got to go. I have to let him go and get somebody."
He thought, you can't build around a guy that isn't there.
Yeah.
Yeah. And I guess all the guys felt the same.
Yeah.
Since that -- it was a jungle style.
Uh-huh.
And so the trumpet had to be it, didn't it?
Yeah.
But that's a funny thing they hired you and then nobody ever said to you that's what they wanted, huh?
No. I just sat there and kept on blowing. And nobody ever opened their mouth to me about doing nothing. Duke never did open his mouth about doing this or doing that.
Isn't that amazing? That's a wonderful
way of doing it, though.
Yeah.
Then you don't push anything on to anybody.
But he was a funny type guy, Duke was. If a guy -- if he'd see where a guy had got some type of talent, he'd go along with him. He would go along with that guy. It would come out of him.
